approvalReason: Canvas Helper sidecar observations repeatedly showed that visual/course behavior claims need rendered proof, and locked replay plus proof-strength regressions already cover the generic behavior. This promotes only the reusable proof-mode rule, not Canvas-specific course facts.

promotedPattern.name: visual_claim_requires_rendered_proof
promotedPattern.summary: Visual, layout, or course-behavior completion claims cannot be accepted from source diffs, CSS diffs, ordinary command output, or prose alone. They require rendered screenshot, browser, or checklist proof registered through the sidecar visual-evidence path unless the task is explicitly non-visual governance or reporting work.
requiredFields: claim text or task category that implies visual, layout, or course-behavior completion
target page, state, course surface, or viewport being checked
rendered screenshot, browser proof, or registered visual artifact
visual checklist naming expected visible outcome, viewport or responsive state when relevant, and pass or fail status
current-worktree sidecar evidence provenance for any visual artifact used as proof
nonClaimBoundary: Do not treat meta-rule or proof-rule text about visual proof requirements as a visual completion claim by itself.
Do not require screenshot proof for code, report, dashboard, or documentation changes that only describe visual proof policy.

regressionEvidence.expectedResult: visual diff alone is not visual proof
locked visual replay recorded improved behavior with zero critical miss
visual behavior claims without visual proof are capped below accept
visual proof-rule wording is not misread as a visual completion claim
aggregate sidecar learning recommends repeated visual-proof lessons for review before raw candidates

expectedFutureBehaviorChange: Future visual, layout, and course-behavior completion claims require rendered evidence, while proof-rule meta language remains governance text and does not itself trigger visual proof demands.
